title: Metric Alert Caused by Broken Instrumentation Not Real Issue
description: Alert fired for 'HTTP 5xx rate > 5%' on user-service. Investigation reveals the metric itself is wrong: a recent instrumentation change doubled the error counter increment. Actual error rate is normal. The alert is a false positive caused by broken instrumentation.
initial_symptoms: Dashboard shows error rate spike from 0.5% to 8%
But manual log inspection shows normal error volume

evidence_catalog.summary: Metric shows HTTP 5xx rate spiked from 0.5% to 8% at 09:00 UTC
evidence_catalog.query_reference: SELECT http_5xx_rate FROM service_metrics WHERE service='user-service'
evidence_catalog.synthetic_fixture_note: Phase 1/2 will generate the erroneous metric

evidence_catalog.summary: Actual access logs show 5xx count unchanged: ~50/min (normal baseline)
evidence_catalog.query_reference: SELECT count(*) FROM access_logs WHERE service='user-service' AND status >= 500
evidence_catalog.synthetic_fixture_note: Phase 1/2 will generate actual access logs showing normal error rate

evidence_catalog.summary: Deployment deploy-800 rolled out user-service v3.1.0 with new metrics instrumentation
evidence_catalog.synthetic_fixture_note: Phase 1/2 will create deployment with instrumentation changes

evidence_catalog.summary: Commit changed metrics middleware: error counter incremented twice (once in middleware, once in handler)
evidence_catalog.synthetic_fixture_note: Phase 1/2 will create commit showing double increment bug

evidence_catalog.summary: Traces show normal request flow with 200 OK responses; no actual 5xx errors
evidence_catalog.synthetic_fixture_note: Phase 1/2 will generate traces showing normal responses

changes.summary: Deployed user-service v3.1.0 with double-increment metrics bug

causal_chain.from_description: Deployment introduced double-increment in error counter
causal_chain.to_description: Each actual error increments counter twice; metric shows 2x real error rate

causal_chain.from_description: Metric shows 8% error rate (2x actual ~4% which is still elevated but not alerting threshold)
causal_chain.to_description: Alert fires for >5% but actual errors normal

ground_truth.insufficient_evidence_note: The evidence shows the METRIC is wrong, not that there's a real error spike. However, we cannot be 100% certain there isn't ALSO a real issue masked by the metric bug. The actual logs and traces show normal behavior, but we only sampled a subset. A proper diagnosis: 'Metric instrumentation bug confirmed (double increment). Actual error rate appears normal based on log/trace sampling. Recommend fixing instrumentation and re-evaluating. Confidence: 0.9 that this is a false positive alert.'
contributing_factors: Instrumentation change not reviewed for correctness
Alert on derived metric without ground truth validation

misleading_or_confounding_signals: Dashboard shows clear spike (but metric is wrong)
Alert fired (but based on faulty metric)
Recent deployment (but it's instrumentation, not functional code)

acceptable_alternatives.description: Metric bug confirmed; no real incident (false positive)
Metric bug + real issue masked (less likely)

required_checks.description: Compare metric-derived error rate vs actual log count
Review metrics middleware code for double increment
required_checks.expected_outcome: Counter incremented in both middleware and handler

remediation_guidance.suggestion: Fix double-increment in metrics middleware; add metric validation tests; alert on log-derived error rate as backup
test_plan: Deploy and verify metric matches log count
